title: Nine UN special rapporteurs warn Fujimori's emergency-powers request could harm human rights
detail: Nine United Nations special rapporteurs — including Astrid Puentes Riaño, Elisa Morgera, Sofía Monsalve Suárez, Leopoldo Maldonado Gutiérrez, Gina Romero, Andrea Bolaños Vargas, Albert K. Barume, Bethanie Margaret Carney Almroth and Pedro Arrojo-Agudo — sent a formal communication to the Peruvian state warning that the Executive's 66-item, 120-day legislative-powers request 'podría tener un serio impacto en los derechos humanos.' They singled out proposed automatic ('positive') administrative silence on environmental permits, an expanded role for the Armed Forces in policing protests, cellphone-tracking measures, and a broadened definition of terrorism, warning these could disproportionately affect indigenous and rural communities and recalling past protester deaths and a UN report documenting chemical-agent projectiles fired from helicopters. Peru's permanent mission in Geneva responded on September 17 that the concerns were premature since the request remained under review by Congress's Constitution Committee, without addressing the rapporteurs' specific questions on environmental silence, military use, or surveillance.

media.caption: UN special rapporteurs question Peru's proposed emergency legislative powers

title: Executive creates a Presidential Strategic Secretariat, drawing power-concentration criticism
detail: The Fujimori government officialized, via Supreme Decree No. 122-2026 from the Presidency of the Council of Ministers, the creation of a Secretaría Estratégica Presidencial that concentrates monitoring and coordination of the government's agenda directly under the presidency — proposing overall government policy, tracking executive priorities, demanding information from any ministry or public entity, advising on strategic communications, and coordinating presidential activities. Two companion bodies were created alongside it: a Comisión Consultiva para el Despacho Presidencial and an Oficina General de Difusión y Prensa. Political analysts Gerardo Távara and Martín Ueda criticized the move, warning that unlike ministers — who answer to Congress — the new secretariat lacks equivalent oversight mechanisms and represents a further concentration of decision-making power around the presidency, dubbed a 'minigabinete' by critics.

media.caption: Executive creates the Secretaría Estratégica Presidencial, September 15, 2026
